problem: Prior VLN agents on R2R learn only from the full ground-truth trajectory. No intermediate supervision links parts of the instruction to parts of the path. As a result, agents barely exploit vision-language correspondence (e.g., Hu et al. found a self-monitoring agent gets 40.5% SR with vision vs 39.7% without), and one cannot check during navigation which part of the instruction has been completed.
motivation: If agents are taught which short instruction segment corresponds to which stretch of the path, they should ground language to perception better, follow the described path more closely, and reach the goal more often. Fine-grained annotations also make navigation traceable, so each sub-task can be evaluated separately. The paper argues the right granularity for VLN is the sub-instruction, not the whole instruction or single words.
key_idea: Split each R2R instruction into sub-instructions with a dependency-parse heuristic and have humans annotate the matching sub-paths (FGR2R). Existing agents then attend only to the current sub-instruction, and a learned shifting module, supervised by the sub-path boundaries, decides when to move on to the next sub-instruction.
insight: Restricting textual attention to a single sub-instruction, and supervising when to shift, helps imitation-learning agents follow the path. On R2R val-unseen, SR rises 29.8→34.7 for Speaker-Follower, 40.7→42.4 for Self-Monitoring and 21.8→22.9 for Seq2Seq, with lower path length and higher nDTW. The RL-trained Back-Translation agent gains nothing (46.6→46.7 SR), and on R4R it trades SR (31.2→21.5) for better nDTW (0.39→0.48). So the module pushes agents toward path fidelity, and the shift supervision can interfere with RL exploration or with concatenated paths whose intermediate 'stop' sub-instructions are misleading. The shift predictor itself is weak (best F1 0.331; precision up to 0.806 but recall ≤0.209). Per-sub-instruction traceability analysis shows agents do well on simple single-action sub-instructions ('exit the bedroom'). They fail on object-referring ('walk past the sink, fridge, oven') and conditional ('walk along the grass until you reach ...') sub-instructions.
method: Chunking function: runs the StanfordNLP parser to get each word's dependency and governor. A new sub-instruction starts at (1) a word with dependency root once the previous chunk is complete, (2) a conj word whose governor is the previous root, or (3) a parataxis word. A Check() step enforces a minimum of 2 words and merges dangling action phrases (e.g., 'go straight then') into the neighbouring chunk. Agreement with 300 manually chunked samples: smoothed BLEU-4 0.84.

FGR2R dataset: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers (58 qualified out of 126, screened on 15 gold samples) assign start/end viewpoints of the ground-truth path to each sub-instruction. Averages: 3.6 sub-instructions per instruction, 7.2 words per sub-instruction, 2.4 viewpoints per sub-instruction (min 1, max 7). Covers the train and val splits.

Sub-instruction attention: the full instruction is encoded by a unidirectional LSTM, and the hidden states are chunked. Soft attention z = (W_u h_{t-1})^T x_{i,j} is applied only over the words of the currently selected sub-instruction x_i, replacing the base agent's attention over the whole instruction.

Sub-instruction shifting module: a gated co-grounded state h^c_t = σ(W_c1[W_c0 h_t, v^a_t, x̂_i]) ⊙ tanh(m_t), combined with a one-hot e_t of the number of remaining sub-instructions, gives p^s_t = σ(W_c2[W_c3 e_t, h^c_t]). Above a threshold the agent shifts one step forward only (monotonic alignment).

Training: action cross-entropy under student forcing, plus a binary cross-entropy shift loss under teacher forcing. The ground-truth shift is 1 if the agent is within 0.5 m of the current sub-path's end viewpoint. An equal number of shift and no-shift samples is drawn per step to avoid collapse. For Back-Translation the shift loss is applied only to the teacher-forcing IL branch. In training, sub-instructions paired with a single viewpoint are merged into the next one.
Plug-in integration: the module is added to Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower, Self-Monitoring (progress monitor removed) and Back-Translation/EnvDrop, using their official code and hyperparameters.

Traceability analysis: per-sub-instruction nDTW and the distance between the predicted shift viewpoint and the sub-path end. Sub-instructions are grouped into 100 clusters by complete-linkage agglomerative clustering on a BLEU-4 similarity matrix.

setting.backbone: LSTM seq2seq VLN agents (Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower, Self-Monitoring, Back-Translation/EnvDrop) on ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-152 features, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: R2R train split plus the new FGR2R sub-instruction/sub-path annotations (AMT). Each base agent otherwise uses its own official training recipe and hyperparameters (e.g., Back-Translation's A2C + speaker/environmental-dropout augmentation). The paper does not state which augmentations were kept for each agent.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ResNet-152 features per navigable direction + heading/elevation encoding); Seq2Seq uses a single egocentric view
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space); Seq2Seq uses low-level turn/forward actions on the nav graph
setting.privileged: none (at test time sub-instructions come from the automatic text-only chunking; sub-path annotations are used only as training supervision)

numbers_note: Only val-unseen results are reported: no R2R test-server or val-seen numbers. SPL and nDTW are printed as fractions (e.g., 0.32) and converted here to 0-100. PL is mapped to TL. Baseline numbers (in brackets) are the authors' re-runs without the module. The 'Ablation Study' section is empty in the provided source. Table 2 also gives shift-prediction statistics on val-unseen (e.g., Self-Monitoring: accuracy 0.699, precision 0.757, recall 0.194, F1 0.309; Back-Translation F1 0.331); these are not navigation metrics and are omitted from the entries above.
results: On R2R val-unseen the sub-instruction module improves all three imitation-learning agents: Speaker-Follower SR 29.8→34.7 and SPL 0.22→0.28; Self-Monitoring SR 40.7→42.4 and nDTW 0.58→0.61; Seq2Seq SR 21.8→22.9. Path lengths are shorter and nDTW higher. The RL-based Back-Translation agent is essentially unchanged (SR 46.7 vs 46.6, SPL 0.43 both). On R4R results are mixed: Self-Monitoring gains 1.6 SR, while Back-Translation drops in SR (31.2→21.5) but rises in SPL (0.14→0.17) and nDTW (0.39→0.48).
limitations: The shift predictor is weak (best F1 0.331, recall ≤0.209), and the module gives no gain for the RL-trained Back-Translation agent.
Transfer to R4R is poor. Linking viewpoints have no sub-instruction, and the intermediate 'stop' sub-instructions of the first path confuse the stopping policy, so SR drops for most agents.

Evaluation covers only val-unseen with older LSTM agents: no test-server results, and the Self-Monitoring progress monitor had to be removed. Traceability analysis shows agents still fail on object-referring and conditional sub-instructions.
